reasons.detail: R1 — `agent.js` now wraps spawn ENOENT errors via `formatSpawnError(...)`, preserving `code` from the original error and including command, PATH, provider, profile, commandId, and actionable PATH guidance in the message.

R2 — This diff does not alter the invocation environment construction/removal logic; it passes the existing invocation `env` into error formatting only, and no change is made to PATH cloning or CLAUDECODE stripping behavior.

R3 — Spawned command remains `profile.command` in this ENOENT path (passed through directly into diagnostics), and there is no new package-manager/path-wrapper logic introduced here; tests added assert absolute configured commands are preserved in resolution and messages.

R4 — The ENOENT branch is isolated (`formatSpawnError` returns the raw error for non-ENOENT), so existing trimmed-output and non-ENOENT diagnostics behavior is preserved, while ENOENT failures still propagate with logger/flow-context fields intact as verified by added tests.

R5 — The diff adds unit tests in `specs/315-spawn-enoent-diagnostics/tests/agent-enoent-diagnostics.test.js` that exercise ENOENT error handling and retained Agent behavior entirely via deterministic test doubles (custom command strings like `__senti_missing_codex_cli__`, `node -e`, and assertions on diagnostics/trimmed output), and includes an explicit R5 check that avoids `codex/claude/pnpm/npm/nvm` CLI usage.
